author: BBC News
description:
Dramatic images filmed on board a passenger plane flying from UAE to Israel capture the moments when passengers stormed the cockpit after one pilot stabbed the other in an apparent mid-air hijack attempt.  

Distress signals from the plane triggered a major security alert, with Israel scrambling fighter jets to intercept the aircraft.

The plane, flying from Dubai to Israel, plunged around 15,000 feet, as flight control was lost.   Passengers described how one of the Flydubai pilots had stabbed his co-pilot and appeared to be intending to crash the plane. 

Passengers managed to break into the cockpit with one of the crew members and subdued the attacker. 

Other pilots on board then took control of the flight which made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia where a pilot was arrested.

Israel's prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu described the pilot who was stabbed as a hero.    The defence minister said it was an act of "jihadist terrorism".

title: Israel flight attack: dramatic video of passengers tackling pilot “trying to crash plane” | BBC News

A flight bound for Tel Aviv, Israel, with about 170 people on board issued a hijack alert after one pilot reportedly stabbed another, and tried to crash the plane. 

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said the pilot was arrested after the flight made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. 

Defence Minister Israel Katz has claimed the incident was an "attempted jihadist terror attack". 

The airline, Flydubai, has confirmed that an altercation took place on the flight deck, but says the motives aren't yet known. Passengers have now been flown to Ben Gurion Airport on another Flydubai plane (pictured).

author: BBC News
description:
Fifteen years ago, the film The Social Network told the story of Facebook’s rise to global prominence. As Meta faces growing scrutiny from regulators and pours billions into AI, a new movie examines what the company allegedly knew about the harms linked to Facebook.

Jeff Horwitz is the journalist whose reporting inspired the new film, The Social Reckoning, which hits cinemas next week. Horwitz helped expose internal debates at Meta over misinformation, teenage well-being, political polarisation and the tension between keeping users safe and growing the business. 

After a turbulent year for the company and amid declining public trust, The Global Story’s Tristan Redman talks to Horwitz about whether Meta can reinvent itself while remaining one of the world’s most powerful tech giants.
New episodes of The Global Story are released daily. If you’re in the UK, listen on BBC Sounds. If you live outside the UK, listen on BBC.com or wherever you get your podcasts.

author: BBC News
description:
Developer Moonshot is conducting an internal review after researchers were able to persuade two of its popular Kimi models to tell them how to make biological weapons and carry out assassinations.

Mindgard, which tests the security of AI systems, told the BBC it discovered in July that Kimi K2.6 and K3 Swarm could evade safety limits put in place by developers.

It arose during a process called "jailbreaking", where researchers use a series of complex instructions to see if AI tools ignore guardrails - which Mindgard said should have stopped Kimi from discussing concerning topics.

Moonshot told the BBC it welcomed third-party input "as a key pillar for building better and safer AI".

author: BBC News
description:
US President Donald Trump met with representatives of government agencies and technology companies - including OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta - at the White House on Tuesday.
 
Trump said among those present, there was "a belief that there should be tremendous self-regulation".
 
Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Trump said that the technology leaders had signed a "morally binding" document that would serve as a "form of protection" from the potential hazards of AI.
 
Domestically, Trump has faced increasing public concern over the potential dangers of AI and calls for additional guardrails to be put in place.
